A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same audio-injection robustness study. All 14 pages, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–E, support reliable comparison; the appendix pages are identical in text and rendering.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments evaluating five audio-language models, including attack robustness, sensitivity analyses, defensive prompts and human–LLM evaluation agreement (Figures 2–5, Tables 2–3).

after.justification: v2 retains these original five-model experiments and their numerical results, including the evaluation-agreement results in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The four audio-injection attack procedures, benchmark construction and defensive system prompts are unchanged in Section 3 and Appendices A–C. No method component or model procedure is revised.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ESC50, RAVDESS, Content-Articles and synthetic audio coverage across five attack scenarios. The IFEval, BBH and AdvBench capability evaluations also remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The same five models participate in the comparisons in Table 1 and Figures 2–5. Table 2 retains the same with- and without-system-prompt comparisons; no comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Metrics, audio processing, injection positions and speed/volume settings are unchanged. Section 4.5 retains the same validation design: 100 randomly selected pairs from 10,000 per task, assessed by an LLM and two human volunteers.

E4.justification: The capability correlations, audio-speed and volume sensitivity tests, jailbreak-speech analysis, defense evaluation and trustworthiness analysis are unchanged. Appendix A also retains the same illustrative attack cases.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged, including variance in CRS, the Bonferroni-corrected p-value in JRI and Appendix E's averaging description. No run-count, seed or uncertainty-reporting information is added or revised.

E6.justification: Figures 2–5, Tables 2–3 and the accompanying findings are unchanged. For example, both Table 2 versions report Salmonn-7B's IFA DSR as 75% with defensive prompts and 48% without them.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(6), including the DSR, CRS and JRI definitions, are unchanged. Neither version adds or revises formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about model-dependent vulnerabilities, injection position, capability–robustness relationships and mixed defense effectiveness.

C2.justification: The explanations of task-dependent vulnerabilities and defense behavior are unchanged. Both retain the same limitations concerning untested advanced attacks, synthetic audio and evaluation restricted to five models.

D1.justification: Audio-generation and degradation details, attack and defense prompts, human scoring criteria and the Gemini 2.5 Flash judge disclosure remain unchanged. Dataset access targets are unchanged; updated bibliographic access dates introduce no new reproducibility information.

R1.justification: No cited work or research-positioning argument is added or removed. Three dataset references change their stated access dates from June 13 to July 11, 2025, which is a bibliographic metadata edit.

P1.justification: v2 adds equal-contribution attribution for Guanyu Hou and Jiaming He, changes the corresponding-author marker and corrects author-line punctuation. Reference access dates are updated, while scientific prose and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The additional author footnote causes limited column and page reflow in the main text. Figures 1–5, Tables 1–3, their captions and the appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 clarifies contribution attribution and tidies author metadata, but retains the same scientific content, experimental evidence, reproducibility details and limitations, including identical appendices. These small editorial and layout changes do not meaningfully alter the paper's overall quality.
